end.summary:
Ishaan practised classifying decimals as terminating, repeating, or non-repeating.
They identified fixed repeating blocks such as 0.333... and 0.121212... as rational, and changing patterns as non-repeating.
They practised converting repeating decimals to fractions using 10x − x and 100x − 10x; examples included 5/9 and 1/6.
They later treated 0.454545... as irrational, so the rational-versus-irrational mix-up was not corrected after it appeared; both skills need further checking next time.
end.parentNote: Asha practised identifying fixed repeating blocks and converting repeating decimals into fractions with algebraic subtraction. Ishaan used the fixed-block method for examples such as 0.333..., 0.27̅, and 0.15̅. One mix-up remained: they called 0.454545... irrational because it does not end, and this was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, practise sorting five decimals into terminating, repeating, and non-repeating, then convert the repeating ones into fractions.
